title: Outpost Source Specification
description: Typed configuration for a single ingestible source. The blast radius of any source lives in this file: a JSON Schema validated at PR time, plus a curated allowlist of source IDs shipped in the repo. This is the contract between the ingestion host (P1, less-trusted, community-contributed adapters) and the registry core (P2+).

id.description: Stable, globally-unique source identifier. Convention: `<vendor-domain>/<package-or-repo>`, e.g. `github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript`, `npm/openai`, `pypi/requests`, `stripe.com/changelog`.

kind.description: Discriminator. `structured` = machine-readable endpoints (OpenAPI, npm, PyPI, GitHub releases). `unstructured` = prose pages fetched via Firecrawl or raw file/RSS.

owner.description: Handle (e.g. `@vendor-bot`) of the curator maintaining this source spec. The plan calls this out as a required field — provenance matters when a config file effectively allowlists network egress.

source_type.description: Closed enum — drives deterministic adapter routing. Per ADR §2, P1.1 is a dumb switch statement on this value, with no runtime inference.

endpoints.description: Map of named endpoint → fetch definition. Structured sources have one or more typed endpoints; the adapter picks the right one at runtime.

extraction_strategy.description: Closed enum — drives which of the 5 strategy implementations handles this source. Per ADR §9.1, this is a declared, human-verified config property, never inferred at runtime.

strategy_config.description: Per-strategy config block. The required shape depends on `extraction_strategy` — enforced by the per-strategy sub-schemas below.

anchor_source.description: Where the version/date identifier for an entry comes from. Per ADR §10.2, this is a config-time choice, not a runtime fallback chain. `url_slug > heading > inline_regex > feed_field > none` when more than one is available, but in practice the spec pins one.

anchor_pattern.description: Regex with at least one capture group, paired with `anchor_source`. Required when `anchor_source` is `url_slug`, `heading`, or `inline_regex`. Not allowed when `anchor_source` is `feed_field` or `none`.

max_inactivity_days.description: Per ADR §9.6 — if the source's content hash has not changed in this many days, emit a SOURCE_STALENESS_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED warning. Default 90. Never halts polling.

auth.description: How the sandbox acquires credentials. Only environment-variable-based auth is allowed in v1 — never embedded secrets.

rate_limit.description: Per-source outbound rate limit, e.g. `5000/h`. Enforced inside the sandbox; the adapter is not trusted to self-throttle.

url.description: Page URL to fetch. Must be https. For `raw_file` and `rss` strategies this is the file/feed URL; for Firecrawl strategies it's the page Firecrawl scrapes.

type.description: v1: Firecrawl is the only browser-based fetch path.

fetch_method.description: Per ADR §2 — `scrape` is the only allowed automated fetch method. `crawl` and `map` are explicitly out of scope for the automated pipeline.

allowed_domains.description: Per ADR §2 — defense-in-depth. The sandbox rejects any fetch whose target domain is not in this list, independent of the URL string. Redundant with the URL's own domain for well-formed configs; protects against a malicious or sloppy community PR that points a URL somewhere unexpected.

index_url.description: URL of the single continuous page containing all entries. Example: React Router changelog.
URL of the index page that links to per-entry detail pages. Example: Stripe changelog.

entry_link_pattern.description: Regex (without anchors) matching the href of an entry-detail link on the index page. Example: `^/changelog/[a-z]+/\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/`.

index_url.description: URL of the first index page. Pagination appends/replaces a query parameter.

param.description: Query parameter name used for pagination, e.g. `page`.

max_pages.description: Upper bound on the number of pages to fetch. The loop stops early on 0 entries, hash repeat, or anchor in last-seen state.

file_url.description: URL of a raw markdown/plaintext file served over HTTPS. Typically `raw.githubusercontent.com`. Bypasses Firecrawl entirely.

rss_url.description: URL of an RSS/Atom feed. Per ADR §9.4 strategy 5, `<pubDate>` and `<guid>` are Tier 1 anchors — no parsing needed.

url.description: URL or URL template for the endpoint. Templates use `{var}` placeholders, e.g. `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases`. Variables must be declared in `variables`.

kind.description: Shape the adapter should expect. `list` = array of items, `object` = single keyed document, `spec` = OpenAPI/GraphQL spec, `raw` = opaque bytes (e.g. tarball).

variables.description: Variable bindings for the `url` template. Required when the URL contains `{var}` placeholders.

enrichmentConfig.description: Optional enrichment for a structured source. The structured adapter reports a version; the enrichment side fetches the human-readable entry (changelog post, blog, release notes) for that version. See [[Version-Join Architecture — Unstructured Enrichment Driven by Structured Lane]] for the design.

strategy.description: Extraction strategy for the enrichment feed. v1: `single_page` and `raw_file` are rejected at validation time because they don't have per-entry resolution; use one of the other three.

strategy_config.description: Per-strategy config — same shape as the unstructured source's `strategy_config`. Required fields depend on the strategy value.

endpoint_url.description: URL of the enrichment feed. For `index_then_detail` and `paginated_index` this is the index page; for `rss` this is the feed URL; for `single_page` and `raw_file` this is the file/page URL.

anchor_source.description: How the version is extracted from each enrichment entry. The extracted value is normalized (dashes → dots) and matched against the structured adapter's reported version.

anchor_pattern.description: Regex with at least one capture group, paired with `anchor_source`. Required for `url_slug`/`heading`/`inline_regex`; not allowed for `feed_field` or `none`.

auth.description: Auth mode for the enrichment endpoint. Defaults to "none".
